criteria.criterion: The change description names the root cause: reading acceptance has no mapping from the request's outcome to governance files, so the omission is found only at admission. The fix is in crates/athena-core/src/reading.rs `check_reading_acceptance`, called for first attempts and retries alike, not in any one job's reading.
criteria.evidence: From reading the diff: the CHANGELOG entry and the doc comment on `check_governance_coverage` both say that reading acceptance 'had no mapping from the request's outcome to governance files ... the omission was found only at admission, after the producer had finished.' `check_reading_acceptance` now ends with `check_governance_coverage(reading, request)`, and the reader path calls it for every reading, first attempt and retry alike (reading.rs:398). Nothing in the change is specific to one job.

criteria.criterion: Run `cargo test -p athena-core`: new tests in reading.rs fail without the change and pass with it. A reading for the request 'Publish to GitHub Pages' with no workflow deliverable is refused, naming .github/workflows. A reading that lists athena.toml but no criterion names it is refused. A reading that lists crates/athena-data/src/config.rs without athena.toml is refused. Each of these readings is accepted once it lists and names the file, or names it in out_of_scope. A request with no matching keywords and no governance deliverables is accepted unchanged.
criteria.evidence: All of these tests passed: a_reading_for_publish_to_github_pages_without_a_workflow_is_refused, a_listed_governance_file_must_be_named_by_a_criterion_whatever_the_request_says, a_new_config_section_needs_athena_toml_listed_and_named (refused without athena.toml; accepted when it is listed and named, or put in out_of_scope), a_request_without_governance_keywords_or_deliverables_is_accepted_unchanged, and the_governance_check_applies_to_a_retry_as_to_a_first_attempt. The tests call only `check_reading_acceptance`. On the base code that function never checks governance, so each `unwrap_err` would panic; this is reasoned from the code, not run.

criteria.criterion: The new tests are table-driven over the keyword table, covering the class (several request phrasings such as CI, gate, workflow, routing, budgets, classes), not just the three recorded jobs. Run `cargo test -p athena-core` to check.
criteria.evidence: a_request_whose_outcome_needs_a_governance_file_is_refused_until_it_is_covered passed. It loops over KEYWORD_REQUESTS, 14 phrasings covering all five path groups: GitHub Pages, deploy, workflow, CI (twice), routing, gate, budgets, classes, checks, configuration, defaults.toml, rust-toolchain and setup.sh. For each one it checks four cases: refused when bare, refused when the file is listed but not named, accepted when listed and named, and accepted when named in out_of_scope. The phrasings are a separate test table, not a loop over GOVERNANCE_BY_KEYWORD itself, but every group of that table is covered.

criteria.criterion: Run `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy --all-targets` and `cargo test`: all pass with no warnings, and existing reading and admission tests still pass.
criteria.evidence: Athena's recorded checks on this tree: fmt passed, clippy with -D warnings passed, and cargo test --locked passed with 1501 tests. My targeted run of reading::tests::a_ also passed the existing reading tests (40 passed).

criteria.criterion: CHANGELOG.md has an entry for the new acceptance check, and the refusal message names the missing path and says to list it as a deliverable and name it in a criterion.
criteria.evidence: From reading the diff: CHANGELOG.md gains an entry under Fixed. The `bail!` message reads 'the outcome needs governance files it does not cover: {path (why)}; list each missing path as a deliverable and name it in an acceptance criterion, or, if this job must not change it, name it in out_of_scope'. The table test asserts that the error contains the path, 'as a deliverable' and 'in an acceptance criterion'.

findings.summary: Broad keywords will refuse readings that don't need a governance file, including root-cause requests that quote introspection text
findings.evidence: From reading the code: the table includes common words such as "checks", "config", "gate" and "ci", and the whole request text is matched, including any quoted introspections. The out_of_scope test is a substring match on the path itself, so 'Editing athena.toml, defaults.toml, workflows ...' (this job's own accepted out_of_scope) covers athena.toml but not .github/workflows. This job's own reading would therefore be refused once. The reading accepts one retry per false positive, and max_readings is 5 in athena.toml, so this is a cost rather than a breakage.

findings.summary: The table test uses its own list of phrasings rather than looping over GOVERNANCE_BY_KEYWORD
findings.evidence: From reading the tests: KEYWORD_REQUESTS is a separate list of 14 phrasings. A keyword added to GOVERNANCE_BY_KEYWORD later would not be exercised automatically.

summary: The change does what was asked. It adds `check_governance_coverage` in crates/athena-core/src/reading.rs and calls it from `check_reading_acceptance`. That function runs for every reading the reader produces, first attempt or retry (reading.rs:398). The new check reuses admission's `is_governance` and `governance_change_is_listed`, so there is still only one definition of a governance file. It refuses three kinds of reading: one that lists a governance file no criterion names, one that lists crates/athena-data/src/config.rs without athena.toml, and one whose request contains a keyword from a small table but neither lists-and-names the matching file nor names it in out_of_scope. The refusal message names each missing path and the fix. Before the change, `check_reading_acceptance` never looked at governance files, so the new tests' `unwrap_err` calls would panic on the base code; that is reasoned from the code, not run. They pass on the candidate: I ran `cargo test -p athena-core --locked governance` (5 passed) and `reading::tests::a_` (40 passed, including the older reading tests). fmt, clippy and the full test suite (1501 tests) passed in Athena's recorded checks. CHANGELOG.md names the root cause and the four jobs, and docs/architecture.md describes the check. All four changed files are on the deliverables list, and the admission.rs edit is a doc comment only. My findings are minor: the keyword table is broad, so some readings will be refused when they don't need to be. This job's own accepted reading would be one of them, because its out_of_scope says "workflows" and never ".github/workflows".
